scope: local RV64 instruction-fetch exact halfword access, execute PMP, AXI ARSIZE/ARPROT, AxiXbar ARPROT[2] default-slave selection, bounded PMEM DPI reads and precise lane fault owner

results.name: arbiter_rob_walk_filters_real_lane1_access_fault
results.purpose: Apply the pseudo ACCESS filter without requiring absence of lane1 fetch-fault provenance.

results.name: bridge_exact_exec_pmp_uses_eight_bytes
results.purpose: Check an eight-byte range at each instruction halfword frontier instead of the exact two-byte executable range.

results.name: bridge_fills_partial_packet_before_fault
results.purpose: Assert packet-cache fill after a successful prefix beat even when the complete instruction footprint is still outstanding.

results.name: bridge_ignores_instruction_rresp
results.purpose: Treat a completed instruction R beat as successful regardless of its non-OK response code.

results.expected_marker: [IFU-AXI-LANE] PTW AR is not an aligned 8B beat
results.name: bridge_instruction_arprot_is_data
results.purpose: Classify instruction reads as AXI data accesses instead of instruction/execute accesses.

results.expected_marker: [IFU-AXI-LANE] instruction AR is not a natural 2B beat
results.name: bridge_instruction_arsize_is_eight_bytes
results.purpose: Drive an eight-byte AXI size for instruction reads instead of the exact two-byte halfword transfer.

results.name: bridge_overfetches_compressed_pair
results.purpose: Force an additional instruction halfword after a complete C/C packet instead of stopping at its four-byte footprint.

results.expected_marker: [IFU-AXI-LANE] instruction AR is not a natural 2B beat
results.name: bridge_ptw_arprot_is_execute
results.purpose: Classify implicit PTE reads as instruction accesses instead of AXI data accesses.

results.expected_marker: [IFU-AXI-LANE] PTW AR is not an aligned 8B beat
results.name: bridge_ptw_arsize_is_two_bytes
results.purpose: Drive a two-byte AXI size for an implicit PTE read instead of the required aligned eight-byte transfer.

results.expected_marker: [ACCESS-G1-LIFECYCLE-RED] RRESP is sampled only on RVALID/RREADY and one halfword is outstanding
results.name: bridge_samples_rresp_without_rvalid
results.purpose: Advance the instruction response state without an RVALID handshake, allowing inactive RRESP wires to affect the owner.

results.name: decoder_starts_lane1_at_fixed_halfword
results.purpose: Start lane1 byte-range ownership at offset two even when lane0 is a four-byte instruction.

results.name: dispatch_barrier_ignores_lane1_fetch_fault
results.purpose: Explicitly mask the dispatch barrier while lane1 owns a fetch fault, even when the slot facts also classify an arch trap.

results.name: lane1_capture_drops_fetch_fault_arch_valid
results.purpose: Explicitly mask precise trap-valid while lane1 owns a fetch fault, regardless of the parallel arch-trap slot fact.

results.name: pair_drops_lane1_fault_behind_branch
results.purpose: Suppress a visible lane1 fetch fault solely because lane0 is a conditional branch.

results.expected_marker: [ROW-FAIL] pred-taken poison lane1 PF is invisible
results.name: pair_ignores_slot1_visibility
results.purpose: Retain a lane1 fault owner even when fetch-time predicted-taken control marks slot1 invalid.

results.expected_marker: [ACCESS-G1-PMP-RED] M-fill then S/no-PMP cache hit default-denies at F=0
results.name: pmp_unmatched_s_mode_exec_allows
results.purpose: Allow an unmatched S-mode executable access instead of applying the architectural default-deny rule.

results.expected_marker: IFU UART is redirected to default
results.name: xbar_ignores_slave_execute_mask
results.purpose: Ignore SLAVE_EXEC_MASK[decoded] while ARPROT[2] marks an instruction read, allowing the decoded device slave to accept AR.

results.name: xbar_releases_buffered_read_without_master_ready
results.purpose: Release the buffered read owner on RVALID alone instead of the master RVALID/RREADY handshake.

results.expected_marker: stalled executable AR cycle1 ARADDR low
results.name: xbar_stalled_ar_uses_live_master_address
results.purpose: Drive slave ARADDR during ARVALID backpressure from live m_araddr_i instead of rd_addr_q for the registered read owner.
